senses: That causes coagulation or that coagulates.
ety: From Latin coagulans, present participle of coāgulō (“to thicken”).

senses: An adherence to a leader.
A group of followers.
ety: From follower + -ship.

senses: That cannot be sought out or looked for.
ety: From Middle English unserchable, equivalent to un- + searchable.

senses: To eat and/or drink noisily.
ety: From Middle English bibben (whence bib; see there for more) + -le.

senses: A small Indian horse or pony.
ety: Named after the Cayuse tribe of the Pacific Northwest. However, the etymology of this tribe name is unknown; it may be an exonym, and may in fact come from Spanish caballo (“horse”), which is the source of the word for horse in many Native American languages of western North America.

senses: A kind of mural decoration common in Ancient Roman houses, usually featuring landscapes.
ety: From Latin topia, from Ancient Greek τόπια (tópia), ultimately from Ancient Greek τόπος (tópos, “place”).

senses: A native, inhabitant or settler of a plains region, but especially of the United States prairies
ety: From plains + -man.

senses: One who, or that which, interpolates.
ety: From interpolate + -or.

senses: The traditional martial arts of the Philippines, which emphasize the use of sticks, knives, and various improvised weapons.
ety: From Tagalog escrima or eskrima, borrowed from Spanish esgrima, noun form of the verb esgrimir (“to handle a melee weapon whether for offensive or defensive purposes”).
examples: Of all the disciplines covered here, the arts of kali, arnis and eskrima, from the Philippines, are perhaps the most vigorous, employing an almost balletic violence to prepare for rough nights on the town.

senses: A device to assist breathing.
A face mask with an integrated filter or filters to keep out harmful dusts, fumes, and mists.
ety: From respirate + -or.
examples: Any N95 respirator is designed to filter out 95 percent of particles 0.3 microns or larger.
The painters in the paint booth were wearing the kind of respirators with dual filter canisters.

senses: The fruit of this tree.
ety: From Spanish acerola. Doublet of azarole.

senses: Something or someone that reduces.
A liquid used in the process of developing a negative to reduce its darkness.
A component used to connect two pipes of different bores.
ety: From reduce + -er.

senses: To phagocytize
ety: Either from the noun or from the French phagocyter.

senses: Any of several large ground-dwelling rodents of the genera Marmota and Cynomys in the squirrel family.
ety: From Middle French marmotte, from Old French marmotte; further etymology uncertain, possibly from a Gallo-Romance base *marm- (“to mumble; to murmur”) (referring to the sound made by the marmot when eating; possibly related to Proto-Indo-European *mur- (whence murmur) and ultimately imitative; compare also French marmot and marmonner) + Middle French -otte (diminutive suffix). Akin to French marmotte, Italian marmotta, Engadin Romansh murmont, Old High German *murmento (dialectal German Murmentel, standard Murmeltier); see also Latin mūs montānus (literally “mountain rat”).

senses: noodles or vermicelli, or a dish or soup containing such.
ety: Borrowed from Spanish fideo.

senses: Any of several other similar intertwined masses of things
ety: From the diminutive of the Latin glomus (gen. glomeris) meaning "ball of yarn" or "ball-shaped mass".

senses: An Italian peasant or rustic.
ety: Borrowed from Italian paesano.

senses: A breeding woodland for herons; a heron rookery.
ety: From heron + -ry.

senses: Synonym of rodsman.
ety: From rod + -man.

senses: A device or person that applies caps, as to bullets or bottles.
A person that makes or sells caps.
A finale; something that is conclusively better, or "caps it all off".
ety: From Middle English capper; equivalent to cap + -er.
examples: And the capper of it all was, Stacy flew back to Memphis to see me for a day and try to settle our divorce with a one-on-one meeting.
The real capper is when St. John starts fawning over Hugh Hefner, host of the finest Super Bowl party known to man, musing: “The question isn’t whether Hef is the hippest octogenarian on the planet.

senses: A wild dog native to Australia (Canis familiaris, Canis familiaris dingo, Canis dingo, or Canis lupus dingo).
A cowardly or otherwise despicable person.
ety: Borrowed from Dharug dingu (“tame or domesticated dingo”).

senses: Having an abnormally low number of platelets in one's blood.
ety: From thrombo- + cytopenic, or from thrombocytopenia + -ic.

senses: One who, or that which, justifies some belief or action.
One who pardons and absolves from guilt and punishment.
ety: From justify + -er.
examples: God, essentially considered, in the person of the Father, is especially the justifier, in respect of judiciary power and authority.

senses: A zenaida dove (Zenaida spp.).
ety: From the New Latin genus name Zenaida.

senses: The branch of sociology that studies interaction between individuals or groups.
A theory in the philosophy of mind which holds that matter and mind are two distinct and independent substances that exert causal effects on one another.
ety: From interaction + -ism.

senses: A fatty substance obtained by solidifying purified beef fat, used to make the butter substitute margarine; also, (US) the butter substitute produced in this way, margarine.
ety: From French oléomargarine, from oléo- (“oleo-”) + margarine (“margarin”).

senses: A traveler whose luggage consists of a backpack; especially, such a traveler who uses hostels, public transport, and other inexpensive services.
A hostel offering accommodation for such people.
ety: From backpack + -er.
examples: We hardly ever stayed in backpackers as it was approximately double the cost of pitching a tent in a caravan park or nature reserve.

senses: A type of loosely woven cloth in stripes of bright colors, used for scarves, shawls and similar.
ety: From Algiers + -ine.

senses: An insect, the honeymoon fly (Plecia nearctica, family Biblionidae), native to Central America and the southeastern United States.
An insect native to subtropical regions of south-eastern China, Taiwan, and Japan (Plecia longiforceps).
A person who is in love; a sweetheart.
ety: From love + bug. From their mating behavior, remaining paired up for several days during copulation.

senses: Both thermal and mechanical.
ety: From thermo- + mechanical.

senses: The practice of taking advantage of any situations or people to achieve an end, often with no regard for principles or consequences.
ety: From French opportunisme, equivalent to opportune + -ism.

senses: A raucous disturbance and/or commotion.
A row, fight.
ety: Recorded since 1890; probably a blend of ruction (“disturbance”) + rumpus (“disturbance, fracas”) - potentially with influence from raucous (“rowdy, hoarse”), from Latin raucus (“rough, hoarse”).

senses: A mountain pass.
ety: Borrowed from Afrikaans poort (“gate”).

senses: Covered with tumors.
ety: From Latin tumōrōsus (“inflated, bloated”), from tumor (“swelling, tumor”), from tumeō (“to swell”).

senses: To estimate the value of something; to appraise or to make a valuation.
ety: From value + -ate (verb-forming suffix).

senses: To hunt for animals by stealth in an area where they are likely to be found on the move.
ety: From Hindi घूमना (ghūmnā, “to wander, turn”).
examples: On off days we went ghooming in the forests and savannahs swarming with game, and picked up various sorts of deer and another leopard.

senses: A glass marble.
ety: From glass + -er.

senses: Other fish with appearance like that of members of family Triglidae, such as certain of those in families Dactylopteridae, Peristediidae, and Scorpaenidae.
ety: From Middle English gurnard, from Old French gournart, from the verb gronir, from Latin grunnīre (“to grunt”). Compare French grondin (“gurnard”), which evolved in a similar way.

senses: Any person involved in the production of video material, but especially a person who uses a video camera.
ety: From video- + -grapher.
examples: Videotaping by an experienced videographer can add so much life to your wedding memories that it is fast becoming a very popular wedding component.

senses: Served with Bordelaise sauce.
ety: Unadapted borrowing from French bordelaise (“from Bordeaux”), from the longer expression sauce bordelaise.
